lesson_title: One Taxi, Four Factors: Who Gets Paid, and Who Gets Paid Last
hook_text: One kombi. Four factors of production. And the owner is the one who gets paid LAST.
clip_script: One minibus taxi, one route, township to town — and every factor of production is standing right there. The ground the rank sits on and the diesel from the well: natural resources, paid RENT. The driver and the marshal: labour, paid WAGES. The kombi, the tyres, the card machine — things people built so you can earn with them: that's CAPITAL, and the loan behind it costs INTEREST. And the person who saw the route, borrowed, hired, and lies awake when the gearbox goes? Entrepreneurship — paid PROFIT. Now watch the money. Sixty thousand rand in fares. Twenty-two thousand five hundred goes on diesel and tyres bought from other businesses — that was never really this taxi's money. What's left, thirty-seven thousand five hundred, is what the taxi ADDED. Driver eighteen thousand. Rank fees two and a half. Interest four. Six thousand put aside because the kombi is a month closer to dying. Total thirty thousand five hundred. Owner gets seven thousand. See the order? Everyone else, agreed in advance. Owner, last, promised nothing. Blow a gearbox and that seven thousand is a minus — and the driver still gets paid. That's why profit is called a residual, and that's why the owner is the one who decides.
visual_style: Pre-dawn taxi rank in warm amber light; four labels landing one by one on the rank, the driver, the kombi and the owner; then rand notes physically sliding into four piles with a shrinking leftover at the end.
mood: Streetwise and matter-of-fact, tipping into a real insight about risk.
pacing: Brisk four-beat naming, then a slow deliberate count of the money, ending on a held pause at the leftover.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never mix up interest, profit and dividends again.
